..
Deep southwesterly flow remains entrenched across the Marianas this 
afternoon, with visible imagery and Doppler radar showing just
isolated showers crossing the region. Satellite imagery does show
some new convection trying to develop to our southwest, and time
heights so moistening of the column with increasing omega (lift)
developing after midnight (more so 2 AM). Thus, will trend the
forecast in that direction (holding off the better rainfall potential
until later tonight). Otherwise, the inherited forecast remains in
good shape with the main changes being to increase rainfall potential
for the middle to latter portion of next week, as a tropical 
disturbance potentially tries to form to our south or southwest.

Marine...
Winds have subsided into the light to gentle range and this will
continue into the first half of next week. As Typhoon Dujuan
continues to move away from the region, a northwesterly swell from it
will continue to subside. Overall, look for seas of 5 to 6 feet to
drop a foot or so by the middle of next week.

Eastern Micronesia...
A weak low pressure is situated north of Kwajalein and bringing
gentle to moderate westerlies across Pohnpei and Kosrae and light
southwesterlies over Majuro. This monsoonal flow is allowing for a
wedge of moisture to stretch from near Pohnpei to Kosrae, bringing
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to the islands for at
least the next two days. This moist air is expected to shift slowly
north, bringing the potential for heavy rainfall over Pohnpei Sunday
night due to increased convergence. By early next week, Kosrae may
move out of the moist monsoonal flow and enter a drier period with
only isolated showers. Majuro will see a slow progression of weak 
troughs moving through the area this week, bringing periods of 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms and just isolated 
showers. For the marine conditions, seas of 5 to 6 feet will persist 
for Kosrae and Pohnpei due to a mix of swells. Seas of around 4 feet 
for Majuro may increase to 5 to 6 feet by Monday.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows widely scattered showers across Yap and 
Chuuk and isolated showers across Palau. Altimetry shows combined 
seas between 5 and 7 feet across the region.

Overall, the only adjustments to the forecast this afternoon were 
for Yap. The forecast remained mainly unchanged for Palau and Chuuk. 
For Palau, tonight looks to be the end of the drier lull as 
scattered showers are expected tomorrow, with increasing coverage 
over the coming days. The best chance of rain looks to be Tuesday 
and Tuesday night. Guidance shows a tight gradient just north of 
Palau with Kayangel potentially seeing heavy rain on Tuesday. Trends 
will need to be monitored over the coming days to see if southward 
shifts in the heavier rainfall occur. 

Chuuk looks to remain on the southeastern fringe of the monsoon 
trough, keeping them in a region of scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms through Wednesday. Both the GFS and ECMWF show a 
developing disturbance near the Marianas late this week. This could 
keep Chuuk out of the convergent surface flow necessary for showers 
and thunderstorms towards the end of the week. 

The main change at Yap was a slight decrease in showers and 
thunderstorms late this weekend and into next week. PoPs were 
slightly decreased from widespread (80%+) or numerous (60-70%). 
Guidance has backed off some with the heavy rain event over Yap, but 
still shows the potential for locally heavy rainfall. The best 
potential is Sunday night through Tuesday for Yap. 

Marine conditions will generally be benign through much of the week. 
The caveat is at Yap where heavy showers could lead to choppy seas 
at times. Otherwise, seas will generally be between 5 and 7 feet and 
slowly falling through the forecast period.
